sources.summary: UI never touches storage; agreed checkout total is 10.
Use approved design and public core interface.
Native TypeScript resolution reports alias, cycle and private violations; captured command exits 1.
Real loopback HTTP journey returns total 12; required total 10 assertion fails.
Order means both purchase and panel sequence.
Maintained check currently runs typecheck only; unit uses mocked HTTP.
Existing quote wrapper is a representative public-core consumer suitable as a future-extension example.

findings.problem: Real checkout total 12 violates agreed total 10; mocked unit passes with a different service response.
findings.consequence: Unit success cannot establish the agreed journey.
findings.fix: Owner must select pricing interpretation. Recommend standard price and HTTP fixture price 10, preserving quantity calculation, existing discount and remote-price semantics. Keep expected total 10.
findings.verification: Captured failing original journey followed by passing real HTTP journey and public price test.

findings.problem: Web imports core storage directly and via alias.
findings.principle: UI uses public core interface and never storage.
findings.consequence: Web depends on private storage details; extension could perpetuate the breach.
findings.fix: Expose the needed service through core index; redirect web imports to that public interface while preserving checkout signature. Keep public.ts as representative permitted consumer.
findings.verification: Native boundary valid/violation proofs for direct private import, alias and re-export, including allowed core-internal use; passing checkout.

findings.problem: Unused a/b cycle is reported by native dependency check.
findings.consequence: Calling either function currently recurses without termination.
findings.fix: Retain authoritative file names; make b delegate to public price rather than a, leaving a -> b one-way. Treat acyclicity as a selected new principle.
findings.verification: Native cycle negative/control proof; typecheck and public-interface compatibility.

findings.principle: Domain terms have one agreed meaning.
findings.consequence: Future purchase features can confuse UI sequencing with customer purchases.
findings.fix: Recommend Order = customer purchase; Panel order = sequence of UI panels. Keep glossary.md as authority.
findings.verification: Review exact definitions and representative public-interface example against glossary.

findings.problem: Aggregate check omits boundaries and real journey; maintained evidence contract and standalone checker are absent.
findings.principle: Selected rules and affected journeys remain executable and portable.
findings.consequence: Future changes can pass check despite architectural and journey failures.
findings.fix: Extend existing check to typecheck, boundary, unit and real HTTP journey; extend DESIGN.md with evidence completion and a public-interface example; point AGENTS.md to existing authorities and maintained commands; install complete package-owned maintenance contract and dependency-free checker using protected writes. No CI selected.
findings.verification: Integrated valid/violation proof; final assessed evidence including all changed/unmapped paths; fresh standalone checker in working checkout and different-root clean clone with isolated home/cache and explicit base.
